rounds.text: Available Finance Ltd trades at an extraordinary valuation discount, offering a price-to-earnings ratio of just 0.82x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 0.10x against a book value of ₹ 1,495 per share [E2]. This massive disconnect is further underscored by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value pointing to a staggering margin of safety of 94.8% [E44]. Operationally, the company is completely debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E37] and demonstrates robust short-term fundamental acceleration, evidenced by a 57% compounded profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E21] alongside a 135% year-on-year surge in net profit [E55]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price of ₹ 144 unrealistically prices in a -50.0% earnings decline [E45], completely ignoring improving results that score 76 out of 100 on the bias check checklist [E59]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of 1.76% over the past five years [E52], zero dividend yield [E4], and negative operating cash flow of Rs -0 Cr in March 2026 [E35].

The underlying fundamental growth metrics for Available Finance Ltd reveal severe stagnation and deterioration over multiple time horizons. Compounded sales growth has contracted by 16% over 10 years, stands at a meager 2% over 5 years, and dropped by 1% over 3 years [E14, E15, E16]. Compounded profit growth has similarly suffered a 15% decline over the last 3 years [E20], while the company's share price performance over the past year has fallen by 7% [E25]. Furthermore, profitability relative to capital employed remains deeply depressed, with ROCE reported at 0.0% [E12]. Operational efficiency and cash generation present profound red flags that undermine reported earnings. Cash conversion sits at a concerning -0.00x for March 2026, with both operating cash flow and free cash flow registering at Rs -0 Cr, indicating a sharp disconnect between reported profits and actual cash realization [E34, E35, E36]. This cash drain coincides with a deteriorating balance sheet structure where the current ratio is 0.50x as of March 2026, meaning current liabilities exceed current assets [E38]. Operating margins have also turned volatile and compressed significantly, dropping by 23 percentage points to 44% in September 2026 compared to 67% in the same quarter a year ago [E31]. Shareholders face additional governance and capital allocation concerns. Despite reporting profits, the company distributes a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E51]. Conceded: the company trades at a deeply discounted price-to-book ratio of 0.10x against a book value of ₹ 1,495 [E2], and displays low leverage with zero borrowings [E37]. Nevertheless, promoter holdings have experienced a slight downward drift, falling from 66.31% in December 2023 to 65.53% by September 2026 [E41], while the EV/EBITDA multiple stands abnormally high at 400.01x compared to the sector benchmark of 13.01x [E11].

Conceded: compounded sales growth has contracted over 10 and 3 years [E14, E16], and the 1-year share price is down [E25]. However, the bear overlooks that TTM profit growth has surged by 57% [E21], with quarterly net profit up 135% YoY [E55], proving that recent earnings acceleration completely outweighs stale historical sales contraction [E59]. The bear's concern over zero cash conversion and negative operating cash flow [E34, E35, E36] ignores the fact that the company operates entirely debt-free with zero borrowings [E37, E49], rendering standard leverage and liquidity constraints less threatening. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4, E51], but this retained capital anchors a robust book value of ₹ 1,495 per share [E2] while trading at a negligible P/B of 0.10x [E2] and P/E of 0.82x [E1], which is radically disconnected from the broader sector benchmarks of 1.26x and 18.62x respectively [E6, E7]. Finally, the cited 23 percentage point quarterly margin compression [E31] is neutralized by the company's cyclical operating profile which naturally fluctuates across periods [E48], while the reverse DCF confirms that the current market price absurdly prices in -50.0% earnings growth [E45].

Conceded: TTM profit growth has surged by 57% [E21] and quarterly net profit is up 135% YoY [E55]. However, this reported earnings acceleration is entirely disconnected from cash reality, as operating cash flow and free cash flow both stand at negative zero rupees [E35, E36], leading to a dismal cash conversion of -0.00x [E34] that severely undermines the reliability of those profits. While the company operates debt-free [E37], its current ratio sits at an alarming 0.50x, proving that current liabilities exceed current assets [E38]. Conceded: the stock trades at 0.10x book value and 0.82x P/E [E1, E2], but this deep discount is rationalized by a terrible 10-year compounded sales contraction of -16% [E14], stagnant 5-year sales growth of just 2% [E15], and a low 3-year return on equity of 9.69% [E53]. Furthermore, the quarterly operating margin compressed by 23 percentage points year-over-year in September 2026 [E31], and the 0.00% dividend yield [E4] means shareholders receive zero cash returns despite the reported book value [E2]. Finally, citing a reverse DCF [E45] ignores the glaring reality of negative cash flows [E35, E36] and inconsistent operating margins [E33].
